title: Landfall and Rivergate
premise: Paloma Whitlock has spent a decade avoiding her father's shadow, digging contract sites in the lowlands while his celebrated expeditions make headlines. When his river survey goes silent above the Landfall rapids, the university hires her as the only guide who knows the Rivergate passes — and she goes, telling herself it's for the permit money, not the man. What she finds is a wrecked camp, a missing concession ledger, and evidence her father uncovered an ancestral burial ground the mining consortium paid him to erase. Racing the first snows through the range, pursued by the consortium's fixers, Paloma must choose between salvaging her father's reputation and burning his silence to the ground. She crosses the pass on the last clear day, delivers the ledger and her testimony to the land tribunal, and lets the law do what she could not — while finally claiming the inheritance that was never the permits: his maps, his mistakes, and the truth.
about_author: August Nakamura is the pen name of a former field technician who spent six seasons on remote river surveys before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who trust terrain more than institutions.

chapters.title: The Letter That Smelled of Diesel
chapters.summary: Paloma, working a salvage dig in the lowlands, receives word that her father's expedition has missed two radio checks. The university's offer is blunt: guide the search party or lose the reference she needs for her own permit. POV: Paloma. Beat: resentment cracking open into reluctant duty.

chapters.title: Rivergate Station
chapters.summary: At the last outpost before the rapids, Paloma finds the expedition's resupply crates unopened and the station keeper evasive about a barge that came through at night. She reads the river like a confession. POV: Paloma. Beat: unease hardening into certainty that something was hidden, not lost.

chapters.title: What the Rapids Keep
chapters.summary: Running Landfall with two hired boatmen, Paloma recovers a splintered hull panel and her father's waterproof notebook, its final pages torn out. One boatman quits at the landing. POV: Paloma. Beat: grief arriving early, before proof.

chapters.title: The Camp That Was Swept
chapters.summary: Paloma reaches the survey camp: burned, raked, professionally erased. A junior crew member, Ilsa, emerges from hiding and describes men with consortium badges taking the site ledger and her father upriver. POV: Paloma, then Ilsa's account. Beat: cold fury replacing mourning.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals her father refused to falsify the heritage assessment; the burial ground under the terrace is real, and the consortium needs it nonexistent before the permits renew. POV: mostly Ilsa, framed by Paloma. Beat: the personal quest becomes a matter of justice.

chapters.title: Upriver in the Rain
chapters.summary: Paloma and Ilsa push upriver by poling through rising water, finding the consortium's forward camp abandoned in haste — but warm stoves and a dropped satellite phone. POV: Paloma. Beat: hunters realizing they are also hunted.

chapters.title: The Terrace of Small Bones
chapters.summary: Paloma excavates enough of the burial terrace in one desperate day to document what her father found: generations of river people, the consortium's claim resting on their erasure. POV: Paloma. Beat: awe braided with anger; inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Fixers on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Spotted by the consortium's search team, the women abandon the terrace and climb toward the range, using old game trails only Paloma's father ever mapped. POV: Paloma. Beat: fear sharpening into competence.

chapters.title: His Maps, My Hands
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a trapper's cache, Paloma studies her father's hand-drawn route notes and hears his voice in them for the first time in years. Ilsa asks about their estrangement. POV: Paloma. Beat: memory as both wound and tool.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Paloma reconstructs the notebook's missing pages from fragments in the cache lining — her father had copied the ledger and mailed it to himself at Rivergate. POV: Paloma. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: First Snow on the Col
chapters.summary: An early storm closes the high pass a week ahead of schedule. The women hole up while the fixers, better equipped, close the gap below. POV: alternating. Beat: the race becomes a siege of patience.

chapters.title: The Cold Bargain
chapters.summary: A fixer, Voss, climbs alone to offer terms: the ledger for safe passage and a payout. Paloma realizes he's half-defected — he saw the bones too. POV: Paloma and Voss. Beat: temptation, and the discovery that even enemies want the truth told.

chapters.title: Descent Through Whiteout
chapters.summary: Using the storm's cover, the three descend the north face by compass and memory, Voss navigating while Paloma breaks trail. Ilsa sprains an ankle. POV: Paloma. Beat: fragile alliance forged in shared risk.

chapters.title: The Barge at Night
chapters.summary: Reaching the river, they intercept the same night barge from chapter two — carrying crates of 'salvaged' artifacts bound downriver as private cargo. POV: Paloma. Beat: the scale of the theft made physical.

chapters.title: Rivergate Under Watch
chapters.summary: The station keeper has been bought; consortium men hold the landing. Voss walks in alone as a distraction while Paloma retrieves the self-mailed ledger from the dead-letter crate. POV: shifting, tense. Beat: sacrifice offered without being asked.

chapters.title: What Voss Carried
chapters.summary: Voss is detained but slips Paloma his own field log — photos of the terrace, taken before he could stop himself. The ledger plus his log is now undeniable. POV: Paloma reading by lamplight. Beat: justice assembling itself from compromised hands.

chapters.title: Downriver Run
chapters.summary: A dawn run through the lower rapids in a repaired skiff, pursued by the consortium's fast launch, ends when Paloma deliberately wrecks both boats in the shallows where witnesses gather. POV: Paloma. Beat: turning flight into spectacle.

chapters.title: The Tribunal at Landfall
chapters.summary: In the river town, Paloma files the ledger, her documentation, and Voss's log with the land tribunal as the permit renewal hearing convenes. Her father is produced — alive, coerced, broken. POV: Paloma. Beat: reunion without reconciliation, yet.

chapters.title: Hearing Day
chapters.summary: Paloma testifies beside her father, letting him speak for himself; the tribunal voids the concession pending full heritage review. The consortium's director tries to discredit her as a trespasser. POV: Paloma. Beat: the law working slowly, but working.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: On the day the old permits lapse, the consortium's claim dies with them. Her father offers her his expedition's name; she declines it and registers her own survey company instead. POV: Paloma. Beat: inheritance claimed on her own terms.

chapters.title: Back to the Terrace
chapters.summary: Spring: Paloma leads a proper, sanctioned excavation of the burial terrace, with Ilsa as crew chief and Voss testifying from the record. Her father visits as a visitor, nothing more. POV: Paloma. Beat: quiet repair, unfinished but real.

chapters.title: Landfall, Looking Upriver
chapters.summary: Closing chapter: Paloma stands at the rapids at season's end, radio crackling with a new expedition asking for a guide who knows the passes. She answers. POV: Paloma. Beat: the wilderness still forgives nothing — and she wouldn't have it otherwise.
